feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Smithsonian Secretary on his retirement and the future of the organization
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Lonnie G. Bunch, III, the Smithsonian Secretary, who announced he is retiring after 38 years of service with the institution. He will step down at the end of the year.

entry.title: Farmers fear more damage from U.S.-Canada trade fight
entry.summary: The Trump administration's escalating trade war with one of the U.S.'s closest allies, Canada, is causing economic anxiety in rural border states like Montana, which counts Canada as its main export market.

entry.title: New report shows the economic toll of ICE raids
entry.summary: A new study shows the steep economic cost of 2025's ICE raids in Chicago. Fear kept many immigrants home, draining the area of more than $1.26 billion in lost retail, restaurant, and sales-tax revenue.

entry.title: Pediatrician recounts experiences treating children with Ebola
entry.summary: Pediatrician Rupa Narra of Doctors Without Borders talks about the challenges of treating children with Ebola, especially because their fatality rate is so high.

entry.title: Thousands of NYC residents sickened by 9/11 fallout, trove of new documents show
entry.summary: Officials blasted past NYC mayoral administrations, Republican and Democrat, for failing to disclose data showing toxic air quality in lower Manhattan after the 9/11 terror attack.

entry.title: Georgia and South Carolina are working to eradicate an invasive, bee-eating hornet
entry.summary: Georgia and South Carolina are trying to fight off an invasive bee-eating hornet that's been spreading along their coasts.

entry.title: Iran war leave U.S. bases in Gulf facing uncertain future
entry.summary: U.S. bases in the Gulf face an unclear future after being pounded in war with Iran.

entry.title: How telehealth abortion works
entry.summary: The popularity of telehealth for abortion has grown dramatically in recent years. Here is what telehealth abortion appointment looks like in Arizona, where abortion is legal.

entry.title: Hank the donkey has record-setting ears
entry.summary: Hank the donkey has the longest donkey ears in the world. His mom, Jennifer Gee, says in addition to big ears, the Mammoth donkey has a big personality, "like a gigantic golden retriever."

entry.title: U.K. to ban trade with Israeli settlements in occupied West Bank
entry.summary: The U.K. is banning imports from West Bank Israeli settlements, saying settlement terrorists are responsible for "ethnic cleansing" against Palestinians.
